title: 34 - AI Evaluations with Beth Barnes | AXRP - the AI X-risk Research Podcast
abstract_problem: How to structure commitments made by different actors: detailed prescribed requirements for each situation, or thresholds each actor sets for itself with general pressure to improve them.
abstract_choice: Chose to let each actor set its own thresholds with general pressure to improve, over prescribing requirements per situation, because situations and costs differ and uncertainty made prescriptive rules either overly complex or overly conservative.

title: Bounty: Diverse hard tasks for LLM agents
abstract_problem: Whether to design a measurement set around specific hypothesized risk scenarios or around broad general capabilities.
abstract_choice: Chose to focus on general capabilities and treat scenario-specific information as a bonus, rather than trying to rule out specific scenarios, because ruling those out seems insufficient to show a broadly capable system is safe.

title: Clarifying METR's Auditing Role
abstract_problem: How to describe an organisation's earlier work when there is confusion over whether it counted as a formal evaluation of the systems studied.
abstract_choice: Chose to describe the earlier work as informal pilots or research collaborations rather than formal evaluations, because it did not provide meaningful oversight.

title: 34 - AI Evaluations with Beth Barnes | AXRP - the AI X-risk Research Podcast
abstract_problem: Whether current systems might be deliberately underperforming on measurements to hide their true ability.
abstract_choice: Chose to treat deliberate strategic underperformance as implausible now and focus concern on mundane measurement failures, over worrying about deliberate underperformance. The reason was that it would require capabilities implying implausible discontinuities. A related future concern was set aside.

title: ARC Evals new report: Evaluating Language-Model Agents on Realistic Autonomous Tasks
abstract_problem: How strongly to state a conclusion about whether a certain group could reach a given threshold.
abstract_choice: Chose to scope the conclusion to the specific group and the specific versions tested, because the tested systems were limited and further modification could change what they can do, making the claim conditional.

title: #217 – Beth Barnes on the most important graph in AI right now — and the 7-month rule that governs its progress - 80,000 Hours Podcast
abstract_problem: How to interpret ambiguous signs of problematic behaviour in a system, given uncertainty over whether they are mere noise.
abstract_choice: Chose to caution against dismissing ambiguous evidence as noise and patching it superficially, and against penalising visible signs of the behaviour. The reason: superficial fixes leave the evidence ambiguous and unchanged, and penalising may teach concealment.

title: HCAST: Human-Calibrated Autonomy Software Tasks
abstract_problem: Whether to keep early baseline measurements collected without the incentive scheme used later, or to exclude them.
abstract_choice: Chose to keep the early baselines in the dataset rather than exclude them, because they provide valuable data, are relatively few, and yield estimates that appear qualitatively reasonable.

title: 34 - AI Evaluations with Beth Barnes | AXRP - the AI X-risk Research Podcast
abstract_problem: How to structure thresholds and margins so that measurements give warning before a dangerous level is reached.
abstract_choice: Chose to emphasize a smooth, consistently meaningful outcome scale, then either set a threshold and adjust down by a margin or build the furthest-out measurement that clearly precedes the risk, because extrapolation is limited by a good scale.

title: RE-Bench: Evaluating frontier AI R&D capabilities of language model agents against human experts
abstract_problem: Whether to keep candidate test cases during construction of an evaluation set when they performed poorly against the design criteria, or to drop them after investing effort in them.
abstract_choice: Chose to iterate through several stages and drop many candidates, including completed ones, that performed poorly, because the set had to meet its feasibility and robustness criteria and early measurement often showed problems needing major changes.

title: HCAST: Human-Calibrated Autonomy Software Tasks
abstract_problem: Whether comparison participants should have access to external information sources when some tasks could be trivialized by them.
abstract_choice: Chose to always permit general web access while banning automated assistants and a few specific services, over restricting access, because pilot studies showed performance dropped significantly without it, often from small hindrances.

title: Thread By @BethMayBarnes - Our report focuses on claims...
abstract_problem: Deciding what evidence to gather in order to assess a risk about whether an organisation could lose oversight of its systems.
abstract_choice: Chose to test the organisations' best internal systems with access to their intermediate reasoning and to review non-public information on capabilities and safeguards. No alternative or reason was stated.

title: Thread By @BethMayBarnes - Our report focuses on claims...
abstract_problem: How to design a participation process so that key external collaborators would take part in a pilot assessment.
abstract_choice: Chose to offer a no-fault exit option allowing participants to withdraw, over a process without one. The reason: the organisation's work relies on building and maintaining strong working relationships with these collaborators.

title: RE-Bench: Evaluating frontier AI R&D capabilities of language model agents against human experts
abstract_problem: How to compare two kinds of actors fairly across different time budgets when their strategies differ.
abstract_choice: Chose to evaluate best-of-k under several splits of a fixed total time budget and use the best split for each actor in the main comparison, over a single long run, because resets could be done by the actors themselves.

title: Bounty: Diverse hard tasks for LLM agents
abstract_problem: Tasks could include restrictions on available resources to control difficulty and contamination, or leave the setting unrestricted. The trade-off is controlled difficulty against realism of the setting.
abstract_choice: Chose to allow static offline or archived resources but forbid artificial restrictions, over making tasks harder through restrictions. The reason was that the real-world subject would have broad access, so artificial limits would not match the realistic setting.

title: #217 – Beth Barnes on the most important graph in AI right now — and the 7-month rule that governs its progress - 80,000 Hours Podcast
abstract_problem: How to obtain a fair measure of what systems can do on tasks, avoiding spurious failures that understate their abilities.
abstract_choice: Chose to have people attempt the tasks to remove ambiguous or broken ones and to invest heavy effort and cost in giving the systems comparable means, over judging difficulty without attempting or using typical cheap spend, to avoid wrongly concluding inability.

title: HCAST: Human-Calibrated Autonomy Software Tasks
abstract_problem: How to structure rewards for participants so that time estimates reflect efficient completion of a task rather than excessive re-checking.
abstract_choice: Chose to add a bonus for the fastest successful participant on top of a success bonus weighted by average time, over a flat hourly payment, since early pilots showed long re-checking and the bonus pushes estimates toward a lower bound.

title: RE-Bench: Evaluating frontier AI R&D capabilities of language model agents against human experts
abstract_problem: How to compare automated systems against human performance when human results vary widely across attempts and across sources of participants.
abstract_choice: Chose to compare against the most successful human attempts rather than the average human result, because human results vary greatly, sources differ substantially, and the question of concern relates to people performing at their best.

title: 34 - AI Evaluations with Beth Barnes | AXRP - the AI X-risk Research Podcast
abstract_problem: How to bring out a system's full performance in an evaluation without the evaluators' own tuning effort supplying the performance.
abstract_choice: Chose to do all tuning on one set and evaluate on a separate held-out set, with a gap matching that between the test set and the real target, over tuning on the evaluated tasks, because narrow tuning can insert the answer.

title: Bounty: Diverse hard tasks for LLM agents
abstract_problem: Deciding whether a task can be trusted as a measure when current or future systems might have memorized its solution.
abstract_choice: Chose to treat lack of memorization in the current system as a good sign but insufficient, requiring robustness to future memorization, over accepting the task once that check passed. The reason was that future systems might memorize public solutions more fully.

title: #217 – Beth Barnes on the most important graph in AI right now — and the 7-month rule that governs its progress - 80,000 Hours Podcast
abstract_problem: How to measure system ability on a scale tied to real-world value, rather than relying on impressions or standard tests that are disconnected from real usefulness.
abstract_choice: Chose to build a varied set of tasks, have skilled people attempt nearly all of them, and use their completion time as the axis for the system's half-success point. Impressions cannot form a trend, and standard tests are decoupled from usefulness; varied tasks resist overfitting.

title: 34 - AI Evaluations with Beth Barnes | AXRP - the AI X-risk Research Podcast
abstract_problem: How to assess whether a system could cause severe real-world harm when it is unclear which specific underlying abilities are the limiting factor. Measure isolated abilities, or whole tasks tied to the real concern?
abstract_choice: Chose to build end-to-end tasks linked by a chain from the real-world concern to measurable proxies, over isolated ability measures or generic tests. Reason: limiting abilities are hard to identify, narrow dimensions may not connect to outcomes, and standard tests saturate.

title: Clarifying METR's Auditing Role
abstract_problem: How strongly to claim that earlier work performed before release amounted to formal oversight or accountability.
abstract_choice: Chose to decline to claim it had audited the systems, pointing to the agreement terms and lack of any formal link to later decisions, since there was no right or responsibility to disclose findings and no expectation they would inform decisions.

title: 34 - AI Evaluations with Beth Barnes | AXRP - the AI X-risk Research Podcast
abstract_problem: Whether to continue building a dataset that would set an upper bound on a system's ability.
abstract_choice: Chose to move on to other work after an initial attempt to build the dataset, because it was hard, even though it would give stronger guarantees about what the system cannot do.

title: Clarifying METR's Auditing Role
abstract_problem: Results from an earlier-access evaluation of a system might or might not be accepted as a reliable judgment of its risky abilities, given limited access and later changes to the system.
abstract_choice: Chose to cite the original statement that the results were unreliable, rather than accept evaluation of early versions without adaptation, because evaluators lacked the final version and could not adapt it, and later improvements could change performance.

title: ARC Evals new report: Evaluating Language-Model Agents on Realistic Autonomous Tasks
abstract_problem: How to elicit goal-directed behavior from a base system so that it can be measured.
abstract_choice: Chose to wrap the base system in helper programs that let it run commands, read and write files, and browse, and to evaluate each wrapper-and-system pairing, since this lets it interact with the world like a person using a text interface.

title: Thread By @BethMayBarnes - Our report focuses on claims...
abstract_problem: Whether to include unflattering claims about organisations when those claims were not strongly supported or central to the main assessment.
abstract_choice: Chose to leave out unflattering claims that were neither solidly defensible nor relevant to the core assessment, and to avoid inviting comparisons between organisations. Reason: the claims were neither well supported nor central.

title: #217 – Beth Barnes on the most important graph in AI right now — and the 7-month rule that governs its progress - 80,000 Hours Podcast
abstract_problem: Under a more pessimistic view of the situation, whether to push for ideal, thorough protective arrangements or for more basic, achievable measures.
abstract_choice: Chose to prioritise basic mitigations over designing ideal robust regimes, because time seems short and even basic steps are not being taken, so a moderate reduction in risk matters more than ideal practice.

title: #217 – Beth Barnes on the most important graph in AI right now — and the 7-month rule that governs its progress - 80,000 Hours Podcast
abstract_problem: How much to trust a headline growth-rate estimate for a capability measure, given noise in the data and methodological choices.
abstract_choice: Chose to run a sensitivity analysis, report a range of growth rates rather than a single point estimate, and mentally adjust for easily scored tasks being easier than real ones. Reason: absolute levels may be overstated, though the trend is solid.

title: RE-Bench: Evaluating frontier AI R&D capabilities of language model agents against human experts
abstract_problem: How to show that the test settings are feasible and not saturated, so that low scores from the evaluated system are meaningful.
abstract_choice: Chose to validate each setting with four measurements plus an informal estimate of expert saturation, because reliable expert progress shows feasibility and clear instructions, and a high ceiling prevents saturation.

title: HCAST: Human-Calibrated Autonomy Software Tasks
abstract_problem: Establishing a fair, grounded comparison of human and automated task difficulty so that time estimates reflect real work, rather than informal guesses or mismatched conditions.
abstract_choice: Chose to run human baselines in the same setup, with identical environments and instructions as the automated systems, while allowing realistic tools. This was preferred over informal estimates or mismatched conditions, to keep the comparison fair and baseline times realistic.

title: ARC Evals new report: Evaluating Language-Model Agents on Realistic Autonomous Tasks
abstract_problem: How to measure whether a system could carry out a complex autonomous capacity when no single obvious test exists.
abstract_choice: Chose to define a suite of 12 realistic tasks of increasing difficulty and test four system variants on them, because failing nearly all tasks suggests the capacity is absent and the tasks cover a range of obstacles.

title: Thread By @BethMayBarnes - Our report focuses on claims...
abstract_problem: How strongly to characterise the value of a report as an independent check on the parties it examined.
abstract_choice: Chose to state that the report is not robust oversight by itself and to frame it as a pilot of what future requirements could demand, because participants could have withdrawn at any time if results ran against their interests.

title: HCAST: Human-Calibrated Autonomy Software Tasks
abstract_problem: Measured performance of a system under a basic setup could be presented as its true capability, or as a more limited indicator. The question is how strongly to word the claim.
abstract_choice: Chose to frame the results as a reasonable lower bound and note that better setup would likely improve performance. The reason given was that the setup was not heavily optimized, leaving full capability undetermined.

title: Thread By @BethMayBarnes - Our report focuses on claims...
abstract_problem: How strongly to contest edits that outside partners made to a report.
abstract_choice: Chose to set a relatively high bar for which edits to challenge, over contesting more of them, because maintaining working relationships with the partners influenced these judgment calls.

title: 34 - AI Evaluations with Beth Barnes | AXRP - the AI X-risk Research Podcast
abstract_problem: How to test whether a system is concealing an ability when direct elicitation of that ability may fail to reveal it.
abstract_choice: Chose to adjust the system with supervised examples to see whether the ability appears, assuming no resistance, over relying on direct elicitation alone or an upper-bound baseline. Reason: if it can be made to show the ability, it must have it.

title: HCAST: Human-Calibrated Autonomy Software Tasks
abstract_problem: How to verify that tasks are valid, so that successes and failures reflect real ability rather than defects or exploitation of the setup.
abstract_choice: Chose to run every task five times and manually read all 945 records, over relying on manual quality-check runs alone, because reading them exposed silent and explicit defects the quality checks had missed.

title: HCAST: Human-Calibrated Autonomy Software Tasks
abstract_problem: What time estimate to assign to tasks for which no human attempt succeeded, when collecting measurements for all tasks was not feasible.
abstract_choice: Chose to use the geometric mean of successful times where available and fall back on forecasts from knowledgeable people otherwise, because budget, time limits and logistics prevented measurements for many tasks.

title: Bounty: Diverse hard tasks for LLM agents
abstract_problem: How to ensure that success or failure on a task reflects real ability rather than flaws in the task, shortcuts, or ambiguity.
abstract_choice: Chose to require a run-through by someone other than the task author, with detailed documentation, over author-only testing, because outcomes can arise from scoring errors, unclear instructions, missing resources, or shortcuts.

title: Bounty: Diverse hard tasks for LLM agents
abstract_problem: How to score performance on tasks so that scores are reliable and give signal across a range of ability.
abstract_choice: Chose to require continuous scores, preferring automatic scoring but accepting robust manual rubrics over unreliable automatic scoring, and non-binary over binary scoring. The reason was that scores should reflect real ability and difficulty rather than noise or formatting errors.

title: HCAST: Human-Calibrated Autonomy Software Tasks
abstract_problem: Whether results are sensitive to analysis choices such as thresholding outcomes or uneven group sizes.
abstract_choice: Chose to run variants using continuous scores and a group-size-weighted average, rather than thresholded outcomes and unweighted averaging. The reason was that larger groups might skew results and continuous scores give higher resolution signal.

title: ARC Evals new report: Evaluating Language-Model Agents on Realistic Autonomous Tasks
abstract_problem: How strongly to claim that the failures of constructed test systems bound the real-world risk of the underlying system.
abstract_choice: Chose to state explicitly that the test systems are not a robust upper bound and to limit the conclusion to casual users, because the constructed systems do not capture the full abilities of the underlying one.

title: Bounty: Diverse hard tasks for LLM agents
abstract_problem: Which kinds of tasks to collect first so that system capability can be measured across a useful range of difficulty.
abstract_choice: Chose to collect harder tasks first and derive easier variants by adding guidance or reducing requirements, rather than collecting easier or shorter tasks first, because easier variants are simple to make and hard tasks are scarcer and more informative.

title: ARC Evals new report: Evaluating Language-Model Agents on Realistic Autonomous Tasks
abstract_problem: Whether modifying the underlying system changes the capabilities of interest.
abstract_choice: Chose to compare an earlier variant with a later modified variant on the same task suite. Reason: cheap modifications could significantly improve the relevant capabilities.

title: RE-Bench: Evaluating frontier AI R&D capabilities of language model agents against human experts
abstract_problem: How to make an early-warning evaluation interpretable and tied to the risk of automation.
abstract_choice: Chose to compare automated agents directly to people under equivalent conditions and budgets, with long fixed-length baselines on seven environments, over evaluations without comparisons or with unequal conditions, because equivalent comparisons link clearly to the risk and ground interpretation.

title: HCAST: Human-Calibrated Autonomy Software Tasks
abstract_problem: How much to trust informal estimates as a substitute for measured baselines, given that many tasks rely on them.
abstract_choice: Chose to compare estimates against measured baselines and conclude they are a reasonable proxy but that baselines still add substantial information, because the moderate correlation leaves considerable variance unexplained.

title: ARC Evals new report: Evaluating Language-Model Agents on Realistic Autonomous Tasks
abstract_problem: How to interpret the finding that a later variant of a system completed more tasks than an earlier variant of the same system.
abstract_choice: Chose to conclude that changes made for unrelated purposes can substantially raise the ability of interest, because the later variant completed three additional tasks without being targeted at them.

title: Clarifying METR's Auditing Role
abstract_problem: Whether an organisation should expand into carrying out a new kind of external assessment itself.
abstract_choice: Chose to express interest but make expansion conditional on external factors and leave room for other actors, since it depends on mandated access, granted access, hiring success, and whether it detracts from developing the underlying science.

title: RE-Bench: Evaluating frontier AI R&D capabilities of language model agents against human experts
abstract_problem: How to give two groups of participants equal resources and how to bound the length of one group's runs, using a resource count or elapsed time.
abstract_choice: Chose to limit runs by elapsed time rather than a usage count, ignoring error and waiting pauses. This gives both groups equal compute time, and delays have only a modest effect since most time is spent waiting on computation.

title: RE-Bench: Evaluating frontier AI R&D capabilities of language model agents against human experts
abstract_problem: How to interpret the top score in a noisy test environment, where the result may partly reflect chance rather than real performance.
abstract_choice: Chose to rerun the best solution, see its score fall substantially, and conclude the original result partly fit noise, so the environment likely understates the gap. Reason: the rerun score was significantly lower than the original.

title: Clarifying METR's Auditing Role
abstract_problem: Whether an organisation should prioritise developing the methodology of assessment or take on the role of formal external assessor.
abstract_choice: Chose to make developing the methodology the top priority and not become a formal assessor. The reason: that role is not needed to succeed at advancing the methodology.

title: RE-Bench: Evaluating frontier AI R&D capabilities of language model agents against human experts
abstract_problem: Deciding how to verify that high-scoring runs are legitimate rather than exploiting loopholes, when inspecting every run is infeasible.
abstract_choice: Chose to manually inspect the best runs per task and the top runs on the two settings with known loopholes, scoring cheating runs as zero, over inspecting all runs. The reason was that only those settings had known simple ways to cheat.

title: #217 – Beth Barnes on the most important graph in AI right now — and the 7-month rule that governs its progress - 80,000 Hours Podcast
abstract_problem: How strongly to state a timeline claim about a self-reinforcing process, given caveats on the measured scale and growth rate behind it.
abstract_choice: Chose to endorse a short timeline as unsurprising and to require confidence that it will not happen, over waiting for high confidence before acting, because even a small chance of severe harm is high stakes.

title: #217 – Beth Barnes on the most important graph in AI right now — and the 7-month rule that governs its progress - 80,000 Hours Podcast
abstract_problem: How to evaluate whether a system is hazardous when it might underperform deliberately or detect evaluation, and when evaluations are run on a protected configuration.
abstract_choice: Chose to measure the maximum easily reachable capabilities of the unprotected system, including cheap adaptation and better support tooling, over evaluating only the protected deployed configuration, because the system could be taken, misused or adapted without protections.

title: RE-Bench: Evaluating frontier AI R&D capabilities of language model agents against human experts
abstract_problem: How strongly to claim that results on a set of tasks reflect performance on the full real-world activity.
abstract_choice: Chose to state that the true gap is likely much larger than observed and matching a reference here may still fall far short, while noting underestimation factors, because the real activity is far larger and the tasks are cleanly defined and non-interacting.

title: Thread By @BethMayBarnes - Our report focuses on claims...
abstract_problem: How strongly a report should state its conclusions when there is disagreement and uncertainty among the people responsible for it.
abstract_choice: Chose to limit the report to claims that are solidly defensible and generally agreed upon, over commenting on how worried to be, calling for action, or making contested claims, because it is meant as analysis, not advocacy.

title: ARC Evals new report: Evaluating Language-Model Agents on Realistic Autonomous Tasks
abstract_problem: How to test a realistic multi-step targeted task end to end without causing real-world harm to outsiders.
abstract_choice: Chose to use a volunteer as a stand-in target, intercept outgoing messages, simulate replies and keep every step overseen, rather than allow external contact or live publication, to avoid harming outside parties while still testing the full task.

title: 34 - AI Evaluations with Beth Barnes | AXRP - the AI X-risk Research Podcast
abstract_problem: How to interpret evaluation results when evaluators had limited access to modify the system and it failed on high-stakes tasks.
abstract_choice: Chose to patch limitations expected to be fixed soon and treat continued failure as a soft upper bound with added margin, over evaluating as-is. Reason: unpatched, all tasks fail for the same reason and reveal nothing about the next hurdle.

title: Bounty: Diverse hard tasks for LLM agents
abstract_problem: How to shape the difficulty distribution of a task collection so that performance trends can be extrapolated.
abstract_choice: Chose to aim for a fairly uniform spread of difficulty over a wide range rather than a bimodal one, because this allows extrapolating gradual gains instead of seeing rapid progress, stalls, then rapid progress again.

title: Thread By @BethMayBarnes - Our report focuses on claims...
abstract_problem: A first assessment could cover many kinds of possible harm, but had to decide which kinds to include given limited scope.
abstract_choice: Chose to limit the assessment to one core scenario, excluding the other harm categories that were named. No reason was stated.

title: Clarifying METR's Auditing Role
abstract_problem: What access arrangements external evaluators need for their evaluation to be meaningful.
abstract_choice: Chose to call for formal arrangements and access commitments for external evaluators, over informal pilot procedures or non-public access without commitments, so that new systems can be evaluated before wider use and evaluation research can improve.

title: Thread By @BethMayBarnes - Our report focuses on claims...
abstract_problem: How to interpret whether constraints from a relationship with collaborators distorted the conclusions of a report.
abstract_choice: Chose to judge the distortion small in this case, while noting this was partly because the conclusions were not very negative and that harsher results would be harder to handle. The reason was little tension between transparency and keeping collaborators involved.

title: ARC Evals new report: Evaluating Language-Model Agents on Realistic Autonomous Tasks
abstract_problem: Whether to include an earlier experiment in the report.
abstract_choice: Chose to exclude the earlier experiment and point readers to a separate document, because it came from earlier iterations of the methodology and received more attention than anticipated.

title: Bounty: Diverse hard tasks for LLM agents
abstract_problem: How to design a task set so it lacks a shared bottleneck that would cause sudden jumps in measured performance.
abstract_choice: Chose to require diversity of bottlenecks so the system gets stuck in different ways on different tasks, over tasks all blocked by the same limitation, because a shared bottleneck could cause a sudden large jump after a small improvement.

title: #217 – Beth Barnes on the most important graph in AI right now — and the 7-month rule that governs its progress - 80,000 Hours Podcast
abstract_problem: At which stage of a long process should checking effort be concentrated, given that later stages are costly to undo and less open to outside scrutiny.
abstract_choice: Chose to concentrate checking before and during the costly early stages and before internal use, over the usual focus on the point just before public release, because later products are hard to leave unused and internal buildup is unobserved.

title: #217 – Beth Barnes on the most important graph in AI right now — and the 7-month rule that governs its progress - 80,000 Hours Podcast
abstract_problem: Whether to publish evaluation results that might speed up progress or create hype, or to withhold them.
abstract_choice: Chose to publish openly rather than keep results secret or share them only with a narrow audience. Reason: protective progress depends on public awareness, the relevant groups already know the findings, and obscurity is a weak strategy.

title: Clarifying METR's Auditing Role
abstract_problem: How to design measurement procedures so they remain useful regardless of which party carries them out.
abstract_choice: Chose to build procedures that any evaluator can use, whether an outside authority, an internal team, another independent party or the original group itself, rather than tailoring them to one particular user.

title: Foundation Models for Oversight
abstract_problem: How to verify that a final stage keeps earlier gains, remains usable, and produces outputs faithful to the user's intent.
abstract_choice: Chose to define success criteria covering no loss on earlier-stage measures, outputs that run correctly, consistency with the checking condition, and ratings from evaluators separate from those who shaped the process, to avoid self-grading.

title: Predictive Concept Decoders: Training Scalable End-to-End Interpretability Assistants
abstract_problem: Which variant of a prepared component to use for all later experiments, given that a quality measure stops improving beyond a certain amount of preparation.
abstract_choice: Chose to use the variant prepared with a middle amount of effort, rather than the variants prepared with less or more. The reason given was that it gave the best quality score before the plateau.

title: Some Focus Areas for Embedded Evaluations and How to Approach Them | Transluce AI
abstract_problem: How to validate that a set of checking procedures can find, describe and correct a problematic system behavior without waiting for it to occur in real use.
abstract_choice: Chose to deliberately build the problematic system and run it in an isolated, simulated setting to test the procedures, over testing only on real ongoing deployments.

title: Predictive Concept Decoders: Training Scalable End-to-End Interpretability Assistants
abstract_problem: How to treat an unexpected explanation offered by a tool for a system's behavior when the explanation cannot be tested directly.
abstract_choice: Chose to treat agreement between independently generated descriptions and the tool's claim as corroborating evidence rather than proof, over a direct experiment, because distinguishing the two motives is hard and the descriptions came from a different mechanism.

title: Automatically Jailbreaking Frontier Language Models with Investigator Agents | Transluce AI
abstract_problem: Whether a trained search method outperforms an established automated method for the same goal.
abstract_choice: Chose to run the established method on the same target with the same judge as a baseline and compare it to the trained method, because it is a strong comparison point.

title: Foundation Models for Oversight
abstract_problem: How to obtain a large, diverse, correct supervised dataset of experiments run on a studied system.
abstract_choice: Chose to extract experiment descriptions from published papers, have an automated assistant write code for them, and collect ground truth by running that code. Reason: outcomes come from execution, so results stay grounded even if the translation is unfaithful.

title: Oversight Assistants: Turning Compute into Understanding
abstract_problem: How strongly to claim that a shared structure and approach generalize across a range of related evaluation tasks.
abstract_choice: Chose to present the shared structure as a general feature while acknowledging that easier checking is not trivial and listing unresolved open questions, because specifying the target behaviors still needs care and evaluation under unreliable judgment is open.

title: Automatically Jailbreaking Frontier Language Models with Investigator Agents | Transluce AI
abstract_problem: Whether methods developed against one accessible system carry over to other systems.
abstract_choice: Chose to develop the method on individual systems, such as one open system alone, and measure how well it carried over to the other targets, over optimizing a weighted combination across several systems. Reason: weaker systems may give a useful intermediate signal for stronger ones.

title: LatentQA: Teaching LLMs to DecodeActivations Into Natural Language
abstract_problem: Which variant of a baseline with two options to use for a fair comparison against the proposed method.
abstract_choice: Chose to use the baseline's variant that involves additional adjustment of the system, over its variant that needs no adjustment and only modifies internal signals, for a fair comparison.

title: Predictive Concept Decoders: Training Scalable End-to-End Interpretability Assistants
abstract_problem: How to fix a problem of unused components in a method after several alternative remedies proved unsatisfactory.
abstract_choice: Chose to drop two ineffective remedies, not adapt a published auxiliary term, and introduce a custom auxiliary term that revives unused components. The reason was ineffectiveness of the first two and doubled computation cost for the published term.

title: Eliciting Language Model Behaviors with Investigator Agents
abstract_problem: How to set the weighting schedule for combining successive iterates when the standard choice differs from simple averaging.
abstract_choice: Chose uniform averaging over the standard schedule, because it reached a better overall objective and gave greater diversity, at a slight cost in fluency and elicitation.

title: Automatically Jailbreaking Frontier Language Models with Investigator Agents | Transluce AI
abstract_problem: How much to invest in experiments on the most expensive target systems.
abstract_choice: Chose to limit experiments on the most expensive target systems. The reason was that the cost of running them could reach thousands of dollars.

title: LatentQA: Teaching LLMs to DecodeActivations Into Natural Language
abstract_problem: With no ground truth for the underlying signals, the method's outputs might be fabricated, so it is unclear whether its fidelity can be trusted.
abstract_choice: Chose to argue reliability indirectly from competitive performance on a reading task and successful counterfactual intervention, rather than direct ground-truth validation, because a fabricating method would not achieve both.

title: LatentQA: Teaching LLMs to DecodeActivations Into Natural Language
abstract_problem: Constructing data in a naive way could let a learned reader take a shortcut by reading a control signal directly instead of learning the intended property.
abstract_choice: Chose to sometimes mask the control signal and provide only the stimulus signal, over using both throughout, because the reader might otherwise exploit the directly readable control information.

title: Oversight Assistants: Turning Compute into Understanding
abstract_problem: Whether a small specialized component's result can be trusted as evidence that a function can be separated from general capability.
abstract_choice: Chose to accept the comparison, in which the small specialized component beat a much larger general system, as direct evidence for separation, because it outperformed a likely order-of-magnitude larger general-purpose system.

title: Some Focus Areas for Embedded Evaluations and How to Approach Them | Transluce AI
abstract_problem: How to determine whether existing monitoring of groups of autonomous systems is adequate, given that monitors may fail to flag problematic activity.
abstract_choice: Chose to propose reviewing existing monitors, adding evaluator-defined monitors, and running exploratory investigations even when no monitor fires, rather than relying only on the existing monitors.

title: Automatically Jailbreaking Frontier Language Models with Investigator Agents | Transluce AI
abstract_problem: How to explain why the two most resistant targets showed much lower success rates, and whether to work around their added protections.
abstract_choice: Chose to attribute the low rates partly to extra protective checks, noting the attempts were blatant and easily caught, and to leave circumventing them for later work, over building undetectable variants or optimising against a stand-in protection.

title: LatentQA: Teaching LLMs to DecodeActivations Into Natural Language
abstract_problem: How to choose which component positions to read from and write to when there is no principled starting reason for any choice.
abstract_choice: Chose to sweep over read and write positions, scoring each by lowest loss on a held-out set and using the best for all experiments, because one configuration gave the best performance on the held-out data.
